subject: Clarify: heartbeat credits, rounding near minimums, and packaging options
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena@brightcart.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: billing@brightcart.com
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on small-call billing behavior and minimums

Hi Ben —

Quick follow from our finance team after the sample invoice you sent. Two edge cases they want to understand before we sign:

1) Short streaming calls: when a request is only 2–3 tokens of generated text (very common for our webhook confirmations), how are those rounded? Do they get charged as the atomic token quantum or is there heartbeat/aggregation across a session?

2) Heartbeat crediting: we rely on long-lived session connections where the client sends occasional pings to keep KV warm. Does Redwood apply any free prefix/heartbeat credit against minimums or committed seat units, or do those still count fully against the minimum slab?

3) If we go with the Dedicated commit you previously suggested, is there an option to apply an escape hatch for microcalls (e.g., calls under 32 tokens get coalesced into a single micro-bucket rather than pushing us over a minimum)? Our procurement team wants an exact example they can show legal and accounting.

I attached the Q3 sample invoice for reference. Appreciate concrete math examples.

—Lena
Lena Park
Head of Finance, BrightCart

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@brightcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on small-call billing behavior and minimums

Lena — thanks for the clear asks. TL;DR: we can lay out exact rounding math and propose a microcall carve-out for your Dedicated commit pilot. Details and example below.

Longer answer (policy today):
- Atomic unit: Redwood bills at a token quantum of 16 tokens for hosted/usage meters (this is the pre-quantized example; Dedicated customers can negotiate a 8-token quantum).
- Short calls: we do not currently aggregate sub-quantum calls across unrelated sessions in the invoice (e.g., separate HTTP requests are billed separately). However, within a pinned session (same KV prefix + session_id) we apply a 30s aggregation window that attempts to batch small responses into the same billing bucket.
- Heartbeat: keep-alive heartbeats that carry no content are not billed. Heartbeats that carry a prefix token count (your client pings with a 10-token prompt snapshot) count toward the session's running total and will be included in the next quantum rounding.

Proposal for BrightCart (pilot concession):
- Microcall escape hatch: for the Dedicated commit (BRI-2028-045) we will apply a micro-bucket for calls whose generated output is <= 32 tokens AND whose total request+response <= 64 tokens, coalesced per session into a single monthly micro-bucket deduction.
- Rounding example (conservative): if quantum = 16 tokens and you have 10 microcalls in a session each generating 12 tokens -> total = 120 tokens -> billed as ceil(120 / 16) = 8 quanta. Without coalescing, each call would have billed as ceil(12/16) = 1 quantum -> 10 quanta.
- We will cap micro-bucket benefit to 5% of monthly committed units for the first two quarters (so we can measure KV reuse). If usage exceeds that, we revert to standard quantization and discuss a separate addendum.

I'll loop Karthik for the exact SLA/billing language so we can include the escape hatch in the MSA addendum. Vanessa, can you draft the invoice-friendly sample math and contract language?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if your procurement/legal folks want to walk through.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Question on small-call billing behavior and minimums

Forwarding BrightCart asks — Lina requested concrete invoice language and a one-page example they can give to legal and procurement. My suggested contract bullets:

- Micro-bucket carve-out (pilot): definition, caps, sample math.
- Aggregation window: 30s session-level aggregation for calls sharing session_id and same KV prefix.
- Heartbeat treatment: heartbeats without payload are not billable; heartbeats with payload are counted in session total.
- Measurement & reporting: Redwood will include a per-invoice micro-bucket line item and a usage CSV showing microcall counts by session for audit.

Vanessa — please produce:
1) A one-page PDF with 3 sample rows of math (call-level tokens, total tokens, quanta billed with and without micro-bucket).
2) Contract wording <50 words we can insert into MSA Addendum A.
3) Suggested cap/phase: we propose 5% monthly cap for Q1–Q2 then review.

Karthik — any concerns from the Dedicated billing engine side? Will the runtime report session_id and microcall coalesced counts in the same invoice CSV? If not, what's missing?

—Ben

From: Lena Park <lena@brightcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 03 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on small-call billing behavior and minimums

Ben/Karthik/Vanessa — this looks great, thanks. Two quick confirmations before I take this to legal:

1) The 30s aggregation window is session-scoped only (we're on a single account so that is fine). Confirmed.
2) The 5% monthly cap is acceptable for the pilot. Procurement asked for invoice wording — can you send the one-page math and the <50-word> contract sentence and we will attach it as Appendix B to the SOW.

If you send those today we can route the SOW internally and return a signed DocuSign by EOD Friday.

I'll attach the sample invoice we referenced for context.

—Lena
Head of Finance, BrightCart
